title: FluencyCraft Intermediate - Day 13

questions.question: Day 13 Practice (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)): When talking about making morning tea (by 5:00 PM), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'The cab driver'?

options.a: He is have fresh cup tea.
options.b: I was having a fresh cup of tea before leaving.
options.c: I am having a fresh cup of tea before leaving.
options.d: I am have fresh cup tea.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "I am having a fresh cup of tea before leaving.".

questions.question: Day 13 Practice (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)): When talking about tracking a package delivery (right now), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'The store vendor'?

options.a: I am tracking a package delivery right now.
options.b: My parcel delivery coming today?
options.c: My parcel delivery coming today? yesterday
options.d: Will my parcel be delivered by 5:00 PM today?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "Will my parcel be delivered by 5:00 PM today?".

questions.question: Day 13 Practice (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)): When talking about buying fresh produce at the market (yesterday afternoon), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'My sister'?

options.a: I am buying fresh produce at the market right now.
options.b: I buyed vegetables market.
options.c: I buyed vegetables market. yesterday
options.d: I picked out fresh tomatoes and spinach at the market.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "I picked out fresh tomatoes and spinach at the market.".

questions.question: Day 13 Practice (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)): When talking about rescheduling a team sync (twice a week), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'My colleague'?

options.a: Shift meeting 3 clock possible? yesterday
options.b: I am rescheduling a team sync right now.
options.c: Shift meeting 3 clock possible?
options.d: Could we reschedule our sync meeting to 3:00 PM?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "Could we reschedule our sync meeting to 3:00 PM?".

questions.question: Day 13 Terms (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)): Choose the correct definition for the phrasal verb 'follow up':

options.a: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.b: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.c: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.d: Check progress on a prior matter.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
'follow up' means: check progress on a prior matter. Example: "I will follow up with the team regarding the report."

questions.question: Day 13 Vocabulary (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'iron out'?

options.a: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.b: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.c: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.d: Resolve minor problems or details in a plan.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
'iron out' means: resolve minor problems or details in a plan. Example: "We need one final sync to iron out contract details."

questions.question: Day 13 Terms (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)): Choose the correct definition for the phrasal verb 'drop by':

options.a: Visit someone informally for a short time.
options.b: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.c: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.d: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
'drop by' means: visit someone informally for a short time. Example: "Feel free to drop by our home this evening."

questions.question: Day 13 Vocabulary (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'call off'?

options.a: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.b: Cancel a planned event or meeting.
options.c: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.d: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
'call off' means: cancel a planned event or meeting. Example: "They had to call off the afternoon presentation."

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 1 (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "రేపటి మీటింగ్ 3 గంటలకు రీషెడ్యూల్ చేయవచ్చా?"
(Literal attempt: "Tomorrow meeting 3 clock reschedule possible?")

options.a: Could we reschedule tomorrow's meeting to 3:00 PM?
options.b: Tomorrow meeting 3 clock reschedule possible?
options.c: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.d: I am needing to tomorrow meeting 3 clock reschedule possible?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
Natural Version: "Could we reschedule tomorrow's meeting to 3:00 PM?"

Use 'Could we reschedule...' for polite professional requests.

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 2 (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "ఈ ఒప్పందంలో కొన్ని మార్పులు చేస్తే బాగుంటుంది."
(Literal attempt: "In agreement some changes if do good.")

options.a: I am needing to in agreement some changes if do good.
options.b: It would be advantageous to incorporate a few revisions into this agreement.
options.c: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.d: In agreement some changes if do good.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "It would be advantageous to incorporate a few revisions into this agreement."

Use executive diplomacy 'It would be advantageous to...'.

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 3 (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "ఈ టమాటాలు కేజీ ఎంత? కొంచెం తాజావి ఏరి ఇవ్వండి."
(Literal attempt: "These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.")

options.a: These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.
options.b: I am needing to these tomatoes kg how much? pick give fresh.
options.c: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.d: How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me."

Use 'per kilo' for price and 'pick out' for selection.

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 4 (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "అన్నా, బస్టాండ్ దగ్గర డ్రాప్ చేయండి, ఎంత అవుతుంది?"
(Literal attempt: "Brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?")

options.a: Brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?
options.b: Please drop me off near the bus stand. How much is the fare?
options.c: I am needing to brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "Please drop me off near the bus stand. How much is the fare?"

Avoid 'how much will become' and ask 'How much is the fare?'.
